title: Open the job's PR early so CI runs during verification
summary: When verification starts, athena go pushes the candidate to the job's PR branch and opens (or updates) the job's pull request through the host seam (Remote::push, PrHost::open_pr), without merging. This way the pull_request CI run fills the fingerprint cache in that PR's scope while verification runs. Any failure is logged and ignored. The landing push and merge stay as today and reuse the same branch and PR. The audience is the maintainer who wants faster landings.

defaults_applied.how: Fake-host tests cover the early push, the failure path and the landing.
Criteria check the push and PR open happening and the outcome unchanged on failure.
One focused change in the host seam and the run flow.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261025-055624-ab95 (the CI fingerprint cache) is already landed.
The user's reply takes precedence: the early step opens or updates the PR, not just pushes the branch.
The early step runs in the athena go flow when verification begins, and reuses the same branch name and PR lookup that land uses.
No workflow, athena.toml or defaults.toml change is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fake-host test shows that when verification starts, the candidate is pushed to the job's PR branch and the job's PR is opened or updated through the host seam (Remote::push and PrHost::open_pr), before verification completes. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A fake-host test shows that when the early push or the early PR open fails, the job's outcome is identical to the no-failure case: the job does not fail and land proceeds as today. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A fake-host test shows that the early step never calls merge. Merging happens only in athena land after verification passes.
A test shows that the landing still pushes the job's landing commit to the same branch and reuses the early-opened PR, without opening a second one. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass with no warnings.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry saying that verification start opens or updates the job's PR so CI caches by fingerprint, and that failures are non-fatal.

out_of_scope: Changing ci.yml or the xtask fingerprint
Merging the PR before verification passes
Changing how land merges or waits for checks
departures: The change touches the run flow and the host seam together, which makes it a little riskier than a typical job.
